description: Discovering, modelling, analysing and improving how organisations actually work: processes, activities and roles, BPMN notation, as-is and to-be analysis, process simulation and bottleneck analysis, improvement methods such as Lean and Six Sigma, and workflow automation. Students draw executable BPMN models in the browser, simulate them with queues and resources to find bottlenecks, and redesign a mobile money agent network end to end.
modelledOn: Dumas, La Rosa, Mendling and Reijers, Fundamentals of Business Process Management
Object Management Group, Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) 2.0
Weske, Business Process Management: Concepts, Languages, Architectures
van der Aalst, Process Mining: Data Science in Action
outcomes: Identify an organisation's processes, their activities, roles, inputs and outputs, and organise them into a process architecture.
Model processes correctly in BPMN, including events, gateways, pools, lanes, messages and sub-processes.
Analyse as-is processes qualitatively and quantitatively, finding waste, root causes, cycle times and costs.
Simulate processes with resources and arrival rates to locate bottlenecks and test redesigns before implementation.
Apply improvement methods to design to-be processes and justify them with measured gains.
Automate a process with a workflow engine and monitor its performance with process mining.

units.title: Processes, activities and roles
topics: What a business process is: events, activities, decisions, actors, resources, inputs and outputs
Process orientation versus functional silos; the BPM lifecycle from identification to monitoring
Roles, responsibilities and the RACI matrix
Core, support and management processes; customers and value

units.title: Process identification and discovery
topics: Process architecture: value chains, process landscapes and levels of decomposition
Selecting processes for improvement by importance, health and feasibility
Discovery methods: interviews, workshops, observation, document analysis and event logs
Modelling quality: syntactic, semantic and pragmatic quality; the seven process modelling guidelines

units.title: BPMN notation
topics: Flow objects: tasks, events and gateways; sequence flow
Gateways: exclusive, parallel, inclusive and event-based; splits, joins and correct pairing
Pools, lanes, message flow and collaboration diagrams between organisations
Data objects, data stores and artefacts
Sub-processes, call activities, loops and multi-instance activities
Modelling a cocoa purchasing process from farm gate to licensed buying company

units.title: Advanced BPMN and process correctness
topics: Intermediate events: timers, messages, signals, errors, escalation and compensation; boundary events
Event sub-processes and exception handling
Token semantics; soundness, deadlocks and livelocks; Petri nets in brief
Decision modelling with DMN decision tables alongside BPMN

units.title: As-is and to-be analysis
topics: Value-added, business value-added and non-value-adding activities
Waste analysis with the seven wastes; issue registers and Pareto analysis
Root cause analysis: cause-and-effect diagrams and why-why analysis
Quantitative analysis: cycle time, waiting time, cycle time efficiency and activity-based costing
Flow analysis of sequential, parallel and rework structures; Little's law

units.title: Process simulation and bottlenecks
topics: Queueing fundamentals: arrival rates, service times, utilisation and the M/M/1 and M/M/c models
Discrete-event simulation of BPMN models: arrival distributions, task durations, resource pools and calendars
Identifying bottlenecks from utilisation and waiting times; the theory of constraints
Running scenarios and comparing designs; warm-up, replications and confidence intervals
Simulating queues at a district hospital outpatient department

units.title: Process improvement methods
topics: Redesign heuristics: task elimination, resequencing, parallelism, specialisation and triage
Lean: value stream mapping, flow, pull and continuous improvement
Six Sigma and DMAIC; variation, control charts and process capability
Business process re-engineering and its lessons
Measuring improvement: the devil's quadrangle of time, cost, quality and flexibility
Redesigning loan approval for a rural bank serving susu groups

units.title: Workflow automation
topics: Process-aware information systems and business process management systems
Making a model executable: data, forms, service tasks, user tasks and business rules
Process engines and an open-source BPMN engine such as Camunda or Flowable
Robotic process automation versus workflow orchestration; integration with APIs and SMS
Process mining: event logs, process discovery, conformance checking and performance analysis
Change management and user adoption of automated processes

units.title: Case study: a mobile money agent network
topics: Modelling cash-in, cash-out, registration and float rebalancing across agents and the operator
KYC checks, transaction limits and reversal handling as process rules
Simulating agent queues and float shortages on market days
Proposing and simulating a to-be design with measured gains
Capstone: presenting the as-is model, analysis, simulation and to-be process to stakeholders
